EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  AUGUST 27, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:13 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Carrie Silvano
Tim Zigrang
Vicki Shinn*
*Arrived at 7:19 p.m.

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 30, 2018
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL noted that the date of the upcoming Equestrian Response Team
training should be corrected to indicate September 8, 2018.

MEMBER BRTIS moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 25, 2018 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS CORRECTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korey Bradbury and Susan Cordone from California Water Service Company distributed
project update fact sheets and highlighted the progress made thus far. In response to an
inquiry made by CHAIRMAN MITCHELL, Mr. Bradbury confirmed that their website was being
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 27, 2018  1
 regularly updated regarding the project’s progress.

The Community Services Director reminded the California Water Service Company
representatives that the Rolling Hills Estates 61st Annual City Celebration event was being
held at The Empty Saddle Club on Saturday, September 15, 2018 and that many of the event
patrons arrived on horseback. He noted that the project schedule shows that work will be
conducted on the Palomino Ranchos Trail around that date and that this would be a trail that
many equestrians living on the east side of the City would normally ride to and from the event.
Mr. Bradbury stated that they would make every effort possible to open this trail for use that
day, but would install detour route signage if it couldn’t be safely opened for equestrian use.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported that a horse chipping clinic and trailering workshop would be held
at the Peter Weber Equestrian Center sometime in October. In addition, she indicated that LA
County Animal Care & Control Department will hold a Level 1 Equestrian Response Team
(ERT) course on Saturday, September 8, 2018 from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. in the City Hall
Council Chambers. The Community Services Director noted that the annual Prepared
Peninsula Expo will be held on October 28, 2018 at the Norris Pavilion and will include a
booth focused on equestrian preparedness.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

PROPOSED EXPANSION OF CHANDLER PARK HORSE ARENA
The Community Services Director reported that the Park and Activities Commission did not
concur with the Equestrian Committee’s recommendation to increase the size of the Chandler
Park arena by 20 feet. In response to MEMBER SHINN’S inquiry of whether Pam Schachter
addressed the Commission, the Community Services Director stated that she did so, but she
did not support the Committee’s recommendation due to safety reasons. She was concerned
about the proposed arena expansion being located too close to two unstable, mature trees
which periodically dropped large limbs and that there may be an expectation to increase the
number of jumps, trainers, or number of students per trainer in the slightly larger arena.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

ERNIE HOWLETT PARK JUDGES BOOTHS UPDATE
The Community Services Director reported that during a meeting with the Maintenance
Services Supervisor a schedule of tasks had been prepared to complete the Horse Show
Judges Booth and the Dressage Show Judges Booth by November 2018. These tasks include
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 27, 2018  2
 contracting the installation of bay windows on each side of the Horse Show Judges Booth, the
purchase of a portable handicap lift, construction of an expanded upper deck and concrete
pad next to the Horse Show Judges Booth for the new lift, installation of electrical conduit and
a decomposed granite pathway to the Dressage Show Judges Booth, and a construction of a
ramp and small step next to the Dressage Show Judges Booth. He noted that the portable
handicap lift would be stored in a container at the Maintenance Yard and only brought out
when requested so that the constant dust, water spray from the arena sprinklers, and weather
did not degrade this expensive piece of equipment.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

MANURE COMPOSTING OVERVIEW
The Community Services Director highlighted a staff report and attachments assembled by
the Assistant to the City Manager. In her report, it was noted that manure composting is a
complex process and that residents who attempt to do so are sometimes contacted by the
City’s Code Enforcement staff because they are utilizing methods which are not in compliance
with City, LA County Health Department, or State Stormwater Compliance laws and
ordinances. Thus, the City strongly encourages residents to utilize the services of Waste
Management who takes horse manure to State certified composting facilities which meet
State Law AB939 requirements.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

2018 CITY CELEBRATION AND POKER RIDE EVENTS
The Community Services Director highlighted the City Celebration Schedule of Events and
Poker Ride flyers provided in the Committee agenda packets. Audience Member Sean
Martin, who is coordinating the PVPHA Poker Ride event, noted that Poker Ride participants
can also participate in a Trail Obstacle Course Competition being set up at three of the Poker
Ride stations. MEMBERS SILVANO and SHINN were thanked for their donation of twelve
stick horses for the new Stick Horse Rodeo scheduled at the City Celebration this year.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS

  MEMBER KEMP reported that the footing material in the trail along the west side of
  Rolling Hills Road was becoming very deep.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 27, 2018  3
   MEMBER SILVANO reported that there were several dead trees on the Rancho Vista
  Elementary School site. The Community Services Director indicated that he would
  again contact the School District’s Maintenance Department to remove these trees.

  CHAIRMAN MITCHELL reported that the brush on the west slope of Ernie Howlett
  Park and the canyon below was becoming dense. The Community Services Director
  stated that he would notify Bennett Landscape and the City’s Maintenance Supervisor
  to schedule brush removal soon.

  The Community Services Director inquired whether the Equestrian Committee could
  schedule its meetings on a quarterly basis, as the Traffic & Safety and Environmental
  Advisory Committees plan to do starting in 2019. There was unanimous agreement
  that the Equestrian Committee should continue to meet monthly, as needed.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

C.  ANNUAL LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS MEETING – September 24, 2018

D.  CITY CELEBRATION EVENTS EVALUATION – September 24, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 7:56 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
